In Example \ref{examples-defos-example-finite-projective-modules}
let $V$ be a finite dimensional $k$-vector space. Then
$$
T\Deformationcategory_V = (0)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\text{Inf}(\Deformationcategory_V) = \text{End}_k(V)
$$
are finite dimensional.

nodes.title: Representations RS
Representations TI
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DVT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DVT}}


In Example \ref{examples-defos-example-representations} let
$\rho_0 : \Gamma \to \text{GL}_k(V)$
be a finite dimensional representation. Then
$$
T\Deformationcategory_{V, \rho_0} = \Ext^1_{k[\Gamma]}(V, V) =
H^1(\Gamma, \text{End}_k(V))
\quad\text{and}\quad
\text{Inf}(\Deformationcategory_{V, \rho_0}) = H^0(\Gamma, \text{End}_k(V))
$$
Thus $\text{Inf}(\Deformationcategory_{V, \rho_0})$
is always finite dimensional
and $T\Deformationcategory_{V, \rho_0}$ is finite dimensional
if $\Gamma$ is finitely generated.

nodes.title: Representations hull
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ET1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ET1}}


In Example \ref{examples-defos-example-representations} assume $\Gamma$ finitely generated.
Let $\rho_0 : \Gamma \to \text{GL}_k(V)$ be a finite dimensional representation.
Assume $\Lambda$ is a complete local ring with residue field $k$
(the classical case). Then the functor
$$
F : \mathcal{C}_\Lambda \longrightarrow \textit{Sets},\quad
A \longmapsto \Ob(\Deformationcategory_{V, \rho_0}(A))/\cong
$$
of isomorphism classes of objects has a hull. If
$H^0(\Gamma, \text{End}_k(V)) = k$, then $F$ is
prorepresentable.

\item $\text{Inf}(\Deformationcategory_P)$ is finite dimensional
if and only if $n = 1$, and
\item $T\Deformationcategory_P$ is finite dimensional if

nodes.title: Lift equivalence module derived
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DZ1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DZ1}}


Let $A' \to A$ be a surjection of rings with nilpotent kernel.
Let $A' \to P'$ be a flat ring map.
Set $P = P' \otimes_{A'} A$.
Let $M$ be an $A$-flat $P$-module.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item there is an $A'$-flat $P'$-module $M'$ with
$M' \otimes_{P'} P = M$, and
\item there is an object $K' \in D^-(P')$ with
$K' \otimes_{P'}^\mathbf{L} P = M$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Lift equivalence module
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DZ2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DZ2}}


Consider a commutative diagram of Noetherian rings
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}A' \downarrow\longrightarrow & P' \downarrow\longrightarrow & Q' \downarrow \\ A \longrightarrow & P \longrightarrow & Q\end{array}
$$
with cartesian squares, with flat horizontal arrows, and with
surjective vertical arrows whose kernels are nilpotent.
Let $J' \subset P'$ be an ideal such that $P'/J' = Q'/J'Q'$.
Let $M$ be an $A$-flat $P$-module.
Assume for all $g \in J'$ there exists an $A'$-flat $(P')_g$-module
lifting $M_g$. Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M$ has an $A'$-flat lift to a $P'$-module, and
\item $M \otimes_P Q$ has an $A'$-flat lift to a $Q'$-module.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Lift equivalence
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DZ3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DZ3}}


Let $A' \to A$ be a surjective map of Noetherian rings with nilpotent kernel.
Let $A \to B$ be a finite type flat ring map.
Let $\mathfrak b \subset B$ be an ideal such that
$\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$ is syntomic on the complement of $V(\mathfrak b)$.
Then $B$ has a flat lift to $A'$ if and only if the $\mathfrak b$-adic
completion $B^\wedge$ has a flat lift to $A'$.

nodes.title: First order completion
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DZ4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DZ4}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $B$ be a finite type $k$-algebra.
Let $J \subset B$ be an ideal such that
$\Spec(B) \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth on the complement of $V(J)$.
Let $N$ be a finite $B$-module.
Then there is a canonical bijection
$$
\text{Exal}_k(B, N) \to \text{Exal}_k(B^\wedge, N^\wedge)
$$
Here $B^\wedge$ and $N^\wedge$ are the $J$-adic completions.

In Example \ref{examples-defos-example-rings} let $P$ be a $k$-algebra.
Assume that $k \to P$ is of finite type and that $\Spec(P) \to \Spec(k)$
is smooth except at the maximal ideals
$\mathfrak m_1, \ldots, \mathfrak m_n$ of $P$.
Let $P_{\mathfrak m_i}$, $P_{\mathfrak m_i}^h$, $P_{\mathfrak m_i}^\wedge$
be the local ring, henselization, completion.
Then the maps of deformation categories
$$
\Deformationcategory_P \to
\prod \Deformationcategory_{P_{\mathfrak m_i}} \to
\prod \Deformationcategory_{P_{\mathfrak m_i}^h} \to
\prod \Deformationcategory_{P_{\mathfrak m_i}^\wedge}
$$
are smooth and induce isomorphisms on their finite dimensional
tangent spaces.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is separated, finite type over $k$ and $\dim(X) \leq 1$,
\item $X \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth except at the closed

\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{O}_{X, p_1}$, $\mathcal{O}_{X, p_1}^h$,
$\mathcal{O}_{X, p_1}^\wedge$ be the local ring, henselization, completion.
Consider the maps of deformation categories
$$
\Deformationcategory_X
\longrightarrow
\prod \Deformationcategory_{\mathcal{O}_{X, p_i}}
\longrightarrow
\prod \Deformationcategory_{\mathcal{O}_{X, p_i}^h}
\longrightarrow
\prod \Deformationcategory_{\mathcal{O}_{X, p_i}^\wedge}
$$

are smooth and induce isomorphisms on tangent spaces.

Let $k$ be a field. Set $S = \Spec(k[[t]])$ and
$S_n = \Spec(k[t]/(t^n))$. Let $Y \to S$ be a proper, flat morphism
of schemes whose special fibre $X$ is Cohen-Macaulay and
equidimensional of dimension $d$. Denote $X_n = Y \times_S S_n$.
If for some $n \geq 1$ the $d$th Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X_n/S_n}$
contains $t^{n - 1}$, then the generic fibre of $Y \to S$ is smooth.

nodes.title: Jouanolou type thing
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E7U}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0E7U}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $1 \leq c \leq n$ be integers.
Let $f_1, \ldots, f_c \in k[x_1, \ldots x_n]$ be elements.
Let $a_{ij}$, $0 \leq i \leq n$, $1 \leq j \leq c$ be
variables. Consider
$$
g_j = f_j + a_{0j} + a_{1j}x_1 + \ldots + a_{nj}x_n \in
k[a_{ij}][x_1, \ldots, x_n]
$$
Denote $Y \subset \mathbf{A}^{n + c(n + 1)}_k$
the closed subscheme cut out by $g_1, \ldots, g_c$.
Denote $\pi : Y \to \mathbf{A}^{c(n + 1)}_k$ the projection
onto the affine space with variables $a_{ij}$.
Then there is a nonempty Zariski open
of $\mathbf{A}^{c(n + 1)}_k$ over which $\pi$ is smooth.

nodes.title: Smoothing affine lci
nodes.statement:

Let $k$ be a field. Let $A$ be a global complete intersection
over $k$. There exists a flat finite type ring map

Let $i : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}')$
be a first order thickening of ringed topoi. Assume given
extensions
$$
0 \to \mathcal{K} \to \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{F} \to 0
\quad\text{and}\quad
0 \to \mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{G}' \to \mathcal{G} \to 0
$$
as in (\ref{equation-extension-ringed-topoi})
and maps $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ and
$\psi : \mathcal{K} \to \mathcal{L}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If there exists an $\mathcal{O}'$-module
map $\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$ compatible with $\varphi$
and $\psi$, then the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\mathcal{I} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{F}
\underset{c_{\mathcal{F}'}}{\longrightarrow}\underset{1 \otimes \varphi}{\downarrow} & \mathcal{K} \overset{\psi}{\downarrow} \\ \mathcal{I} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{G}
\overset{c_{\mathcal{G}'}}{\longrightarrow} & \mathcal{L}\end{array}
$$
is commutative.
\item The set of $\mathcal{O}'$-module
maps $\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$ compatible with $\varphi$
and $\psi$ is, if nonempty, a principal homogeneous space under
$\Hom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{L})$.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}

\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F}'$

$$

\mathcal{I} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{F} \to
\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F}'

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$ be a morphism of
ringed topoi. Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}(\Sh(\mathcal{C}'_1), \mathcal{O}'_1) \underset{h}{\longrightarrow}\underset{f'_1}{\downarrow} & (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'_2), \mathcal{O}'_2) \underset{f'_2}{\downarrow} \\ (\Sh(\mathcal{B}'_1), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'_1}) \longrightarrow & (\Sh(\mathcal{B}'_2), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'_2})\end{array}
$$
where $h$ is a morphism of first order thickenings
of $(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$, the lower horizontal arrow
is a morphism of first order thickenings of
$(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$, each $f'_i$ restricts
to $f$, both pairs $(f, f_i')$ are strict morphisms of thickenings, and
both $f'_i$ are flat. Finally, let $\mathcal{F}$ be an
$\mathcal{O}$-module flat over $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}$.

\Ext^2_\mathcal{O}(
\mathcal{F}, f^*\mathcal{J}_2 \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{F})
\to \Ext^2_\mathcal{O}(
\mathcal{F}, f^*\mathcal{J}_1 \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{F})

nodes.title: Situation: Ses flat thickenings ringed topoi
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08VX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08VX}}



Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$ be a morphism of
ringed topoi. Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}(\Sh(\mathcal{C}'_1), \mathcal{O}'_1) \underset{h}{\longrightarrow}\underset{f'_1}{\downarrow} & (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'_2), \mathcal{O}'_2) \longrightarrow\underset{f'_2}{\downarrow} & (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'_3), \mathcal{O}'_3) \underset{f'_3}{\downarrow} \\ (\Sh(\mathcal{B}'_1), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'_1}) \longrightarrow & (\Sh(\mathcal{B}'_2), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'_2}) \longrightarrow & (\Sh(\mathcal{B}'_3), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'_3})\end{array}
$$
where (a) the top row is a short exact sequence of first order thickenings
of $(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$, (b) the lower row is a short exact
sequence of first order thickenings of
$(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$, (c) each $f'_i$ restricts
to $f$, (d) each pair $(f, f_i')$ is a strict morphism of thickenings, and
(e) each $f'_i$ is flat. Finally, let $\mathcal{F}'_2$ be an
$\mathcal{O}'_2$-module flat over $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'_2}$ and
set $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}'_2 \otimes \mathcal{O}$. Let
$\pi : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'_1), \mathcal{O}'_1) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O})$ be the canonical splitting
(Remark \ref{defos-remark-short-exact-sequence-thickenings-ringed-topoi}).

nodes.title: Extensions of relative ringed topoi
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GQ5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0GQ5}}


Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$ be a morphism of
ringed topoi. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}$-module.
The set of isomorphism classes of extensions of
$f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}$-algebras
$$
0 \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{O}' \to \mathcal{O} \to 0
$$
where $\mathcal{G}$ is an ideal of square zero\footnote{In other words,
the set of isomorphism classes of first order thickenings
$i : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}')$
over $(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$ endowed with an isomorphism
$\mathcal{G} \to \Ker(i^\sharp)$ of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.}

$\Ext^1_\mathcal{O}(\NL_{\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}}, \mathcal{G})$.

nodes.title: Extensions of relative ringed topoi functorial
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GQ7}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0GQ7}}



Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$ and
$g : (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C})$ be morphisms
of ringed topoi. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-module.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-module. Let
$c : g^*\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-linear
map. Finally, consider
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)]
$0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'} \to
\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C} \to 0$
an extension of $f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}$-algebras
corresponding to
$\xi \in \Ext^1_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}}(
\NL_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}/\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}}, \mathcal{F})$, and
\item[(b)]
$0 \to \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'} \to
\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D} \to 0$
an extension of $g^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}$-algebras
corresponding to
$\zeta \in \Ext^1_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}}(
\NL_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}/\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}}, \mathcal{G})$.
\end{enumerate}
See Lemma \ref{defos-lemma-extensions-of-relative-ringed-topoi}.
Then there is a morphism
$$
g' :
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})
\longrightarrow
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'})
$$
of ringed topoi over $(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$
compatible with $g$ and $c$ if and only if $\xi$ and $\zeta$
map to the same element of
$\Ext^1_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}}(
Lg^*\NL_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}/\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}}, \mathcal{G})$.

nodes.title: Parametrize solutions ringed topoi
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GQ9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0GQ9}}



Let $t : (\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{B}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'})$,
$\mathcal{J} = \Ker(t^\sharp)$,
$f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{B}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B})$, $\mathcal{G}$, and
$c : \mathcal{J} \to \mathcal{G}$ be as in
(\ref{equation-to-solve-ringed-topoi}).
Denote $\xi \in \Ext^1_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}}(
\NL_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'}}, \mathcal{J})$
the element corresponding to the extension $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'}$
of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}$ by $\mathcal{J}$ via
Lemma \ref{defos-lemma-extensions-of-relative-ringed-topoi}.
The set of isomorphism classes of solutions is canonically bijective

$$
\Ext^1_\mathcal{O}(\NL_{\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'}},
\mathcal{G})\to
\Ext^1_\mathcal{O}(
Lf^*\NL_{\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{B}'}}, \mathcal{G})

If there exists a flat morphism $f' : X' \to Y'$ of algebraic spaces over $S$
and an isomorphsm $a : X \to X' \times_{Y'} Y$ over $Y$, then

\item the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(f' : X' \to Y', a)$ is

$\Ext^1_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\NL_{X/Y}, f^*\mathcal{C}_{Y/Y'})$, and
\item the set of automorphisms of $\varphi : X' \to X'$
over $Y'$ which reduce to the identity on $X' \times_{Y'} Y$

(Derived Categories of Spaces, Section
\ref{spaces-perfect-section-better-coherator})
is an isomorphism. Then the functor $F$ is an equivalence of categories.

nodes.title: Thickening over thickening space quasi coherent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D3Q}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0D3Q}}


In the situation above assume that $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
and that $DQ_X(\mathcal{F}) \to DQ_X(\mathcal{G})$
(Derived Categories of Spaces, Section
\ref{spaces-perfect-section-better-coherator})
is an isomorphism. Then the functor $FT$ is an equivalence of categories.

nodes.title: Canonical class algebra
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DYR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DYR}}


Let $R' \to R$ be a surjection of rings whose kernel is an ideal
$I$ of square zero. For every $K \in D^-(R)$ there is a canonical
map
$$
\omega(K) : K \longrightarrow K \otimes_R^\mathbf{L} I[2]
$$
in $D(R)$ with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega(K) = 0$ if and only if there exists
$K' \in D(R')$ with $K' \otimes_{R'}^\mathbf{L} R = K$,
\item given $K \to L$ in $D^-(R)$ the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}K \downarrow\underset{\omega(K)}{\longrightarrow} &  & K \otimes^\mathbf{L}_R I[2] \downarrow \\ L \overset{\omega(L)}{\longrightarrow} &  & L \otimes^\mathbf{L}_R I[2]\end{array}
$$
commutes, and
\item formation of $\omega(K)$ is compatible with ring maps $R' \to S'$
(see proof for a precise statement).
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Lift complex
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DIT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DIT}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}_0$
be a surjection of sheaves of rings. Assume given the following data
\begin{enumerate}
\item flat $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{G}^n$,
\item maps of $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{G}^n \to \mathcal{G}^{n + 1}$,
\item a complex $\mathcal{K}_0^\bullet$ of $\mathcal{O}_0$-modules,
\item maps of $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{G}^n \to \mathcal{K}_0^n$
\end{enumerate}
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $H^n(\mathcal{K}_0^\bullet) = 0$ for $n \gg 0$,
\item[(b)] $\mathcal{G}^n = 0$ for $n \gg 0$,
\item[(c)] with
$\mathcal{G}^n_0 = \mathcal{G}^n \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{O}_0$
the induced maps determine a complex $\mathcal{G}_0^\bullet$ and a map
of complexes $\mathcal{G}_0^\bullet \to \mathcal{K}_0^\bullet$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exist
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(\romannumeral1)]
flat $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{F}^n$,
\item[(\romannumeral2)]
maps of $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{F}^n \to \mathcal{F}^{n + 1}$,
\item[(\romannumeral3)]
maps of $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{F}^n \to \mathcal{K}_0^n$,
\item[(\romannumeral4)]
maps of $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{G}^n \to \mathcal{F}^n$,
\end{enumerate}
such that $\mathcal{F}^n = 0$ for $n \gg 0$, such that the diagrams
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\mathcal{G}^n \longrightarrow\downarrow & \mathcal{G}^{n + 1} \downarrow \\ \mathcal{F}^n \longrightarrow & \mathcal{F}^{n + 1}\end{array}
$$
commute for all $n$, such that the composition
$\mathcal{G}^n \to \mathcal{F}^n \to \mathcal{K}_0^n$
is the given map $\mathcal{G}^n \to \mathcal{K}_0^n$, and such that with
$\mathcal{F}^n_0 = \mathcal{F}^n \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{O}_0$
we obtain a complex $\mathcal{F}_0^\bullet$ and map of complexes
$\mathcal{F}_0^\bullet \to \mathcal{K}_0^\bullet$ which is a
quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.title: Canonical class
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DIU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DIU}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}_0$
be a surjection of sheaves of rings whose kernel is an ideal sheaf
$\mathcal{I}$ of square zero. For every object
$K_0$ in $D^-(\mathcal{O}_0)$ there is a canonical map
$$
\omega(K_0) :
K_0 \longrightarrow
K_0 \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_0}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{I}[2]
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_0)$ such that for any map
$K_0 \to L_0$ in $D^-(\mathcal{O}_0)$ the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}K_0 \downarrow\underset{\omega(K_0)}{\longrightarrow} &  & (K_0 \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_0} \mathcal{I})[2] \downarrow \\ L_0 \overset{\omega(L_0)}{\longrightarrow} &  & (L_0 \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_0} \mathcal{I})[2]\end{array}
$$
commutes.

nodes.title: Induced map
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DIV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DIV}}


Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\alpha : K \to L$ be a map of $D^-(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Let $n \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $H^i(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for $i \geq n$,
then $H^i(\alpha \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \text{id}_\mathcal{F})$
is an isomorphism for $i \geq n$.
\item If $H^i(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for $i > n$
and surjective for $i = n$,
then $H^i(\alpha \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \text{id}_\mathcal{F})$
is an isomorphism for $i > n$ and surjective for $i = n$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Canonical class obstruction
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DIW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DIW}}



Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}_0$
be a surjection of sheaves of rings whose kernel is an ideal sheaf
$\mathcal{I}$ of square zero. For every object
$K_0$ in $D^-(\mathcal{O}_0)$ the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item  the class
$\omega(K_0) \in
\Ext^2_{\mathcal{O}_0}(K_0, K_0 \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_0} \mathcal{I})$
constructed in Lemma \ref{defos-lemma-canonical-class} is zero,
\item there exists $K \in D^-(\mathcal{O})$ with
$K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}_0 = K_0$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_0)$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Lift map complexes
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DIX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DIX}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}_0$
be a surjection of sheaves of rings. Assume given the following data
\begin{enumerate}
\item a complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$,
\item a complex $\mathcal{K}_0^\bullet$ of $\mathcal{O}_0$-modules,
\item a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal{K}_0^\bullet \to
\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{O}_0$,
\end{enumerate}
Then there exist a quasi-isomorphism
$\mathcal{G}^\bullet \to \mathcal{F}^\bullet$ such that the map
of complexes
$\mathcal{G}^\bullet  \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{O}_0 \to
\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{O}_0$ factors
through $\mathcal{K}_0^\bullet$ in the homotopy category
of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_0$-modules.

nodes.title: Inf obs map defo complex
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DIY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DIY}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}_0$
be a surjection of sheaves of rings whose kernel is an ideal sheaf
$\mathcal{I}$ of square zero. Let $K, L \in D^-(\mathcal{O})$.
Set $K_0 = K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}_0$
and $L_0 = L \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}_0$
in $D^-(\mathcal{O}_0)$. Given $\alpha_0 : K_0 \to L_0$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_0)$
there is a canonical element
$$
o(\alpha_0) \in \Ext^1_{\mathcal{O}_0}(K_0,
L_0 \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_0}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{I})
$$
whose vanishing is necessary and sufficient for the
existence of a map $\alpha : K \to L$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$
with $\alpha_0 = \alpha \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \text{id}$.

nodes.title: First order defos complex
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DIZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DIZ}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}_0$
be a surjection of sheaves of rings whose kernel is an ideal sheaf
$\mathcal{I}$ of square zero. Let $K_0 \in D^-(\mathcal{O})$.
A lift of $K_0$ is a pair $(K, \alpha_0)$ consisting of an object
$K$ in $D^-(\mathcal{O})$ and an isomorphism
$\alpha_0 : K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}_0 \to K_0$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_0)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Given a lift $(K, \alpha)$ the group of automorphism of the pair
is canonically the cokernel of a map
$$
\Ext^{-1}_{\mathcal{O}_0}(K_0, K_0)
\longrightarrow
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_0}(K_0, K_0 \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_0}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{I})
$$
\item If there is a lift, then the set of isomorphism classes of lifts
is principal homogenenous under
$\Ext^1_{\mathcal{O}_0}(K_0,
K_0 \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_0}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{I})$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: CLambda
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06GC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06GC}}


Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let $\Lambda \to k$ be a finite
ring map where $k$ is a field. We define {\it $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$} to be
the category with
\begin{enumerate}
\item objects are pairs $(A, \varphi)$ where $A$ is an Artinian local
$\Lambda$-algebra and where $\varphi : A/\mathfrak m_A \to k$ is a
$\Lambda$-algebra isomorphism, and
\item morphisms $f : (B, \psi) \to (A, \varphi)$ are local $\Lambda$-algebra
homomorphisms such that $\varphi \circ (f \bmod \mathfrak m) = \psi$.
\end{enumerate}
We say we are in the {\it classical case} if $\Lambda$ is a Noetherian
complete local ring and $k$ is its residue field.

nodes.title: Small extension
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06GD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06GD}}


Let $f: B \to A$ be a ring map in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.  We say $f$
is a {\it small extension} if it is surjective and $\Ker(f)$ is a nonzero
principal ideal which is annihilated by $\mathfrak{m}_B$.

nodes.title: Factor small extension
Length
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06GG}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06GG}}


Let $A$ be a local $\Lambda$-algebra with residue field $k$.
Let $M$ be an $A$-module. Then
$[k : k'] \text{length}_A(M) = \text{length}_\Lambda(M)$.
In the classical case we have
$\text{length}_A(M) = \text{length}_\Lambda(M)$.

nodes.title: Surjective
Tangent space ring
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06GY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06GY}}


Let $R \to S$ be a local homomorphism of local rings. The
{\it relative cotangent space}\footnote{Caution: We will see later
that in our general setting the tangent
space of an object $A \in \mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ over $\Lambda$ should
not be defined simply as the $k$-linear dual of the relative
cotangent space. In fact, the correct definition of the relative
cotangent space is
$\Omega_{S/R} \otimes_S S/\mathfrak m_S$.} of $R$ over $S$ is the
$S/\mathfrak m_S$-vector space
$\mathfrak m_S/(\mathfrak m_R S + \mathfrak m_S^2)$.

nodes.title: Fiber product CLambda
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06GH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06GH}}


Let $f_1 : A_1 \to A$ and $f_2 : A_2 \to A$ be ring maps in
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f_1$ or $f_2$ is surjective, then
$A_1 \times_A A_2$ is in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.
\item If $f_2$ is a small extension, then so is
$A_1 \times_A A_2 \to A_1$.
\item If the field extension $k/k'$ is separable, then
$A_1 \times_A A_2$ is in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Essential surjection
Essential surjection mod squares
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06S5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06S5}}


Let $f: B \to A$ be a ring map in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is an essential surjection,
\item the map $B/\mathfrak m_B^2 \to A/\mathfrak m_A^2$ is an essential
surjection, and
\item the map
$B/(\mathfrak m_\Lambda B + \mathfrak m_B^2) \to
A/(\mathfrak m_\Lambda A + \mathfrak m_A^2)$ is an essential surjection.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: H1 separable case
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06S9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06S9}}


There is a canonical map
$$
\mathfrak m_\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda^2 \longrightarrow H_1(L_{k/\Lambda}).
$$
If $k' \subset k$ is separable (for example if the characteristic
of $k$ is zero), then this map induces an isomorphism
$\mathfrak m_\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda^2 \otimes_{k'} k = H_1(L_{k/\Lambda})$.
If $k = k'$ (for example in the classical case), then
$\mathfrak m_\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda^2 = H_1(L_{k/\Lambda})$.
The composition
$$
\mathfrak m_\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda^2 \longrightarrow
H_1(L_{k/\Lambda}) \longrightarrow \mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2
$$
comes from the canonical map $\mathfrak m_\Lambda \to \mathfrak m_A$.

nodes.title: Essential surjection
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06H0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06H0}}


Let $f: B \to A$ be a ring map in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.
Notation as in (\ref{equation-sequence-functorial}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item The equivalent conditions of
Lemma \ref{formal-defos-lemma-surjective}
characterizing when $f$ is surjective are also equivalent to
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Im(\text{d}_B) \to \Im(\text{d}_A)$ is surjective, and
\item the map $\Omega_{B/\Lambda} \otimes_B k \to
\Omega_{A/\Lambda} \otimes_A k$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
\item The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is an essential surjection
(see Lemma \ref{formal-defos-lemma-essential-surjection-mod-squares}),
\item the map $\Im(\text{d}_B) \to \Im(\text{d}_A)$ is an
isomorphism, and
\item the map $\Omega_{B/\Lambda} \otimes_B k \to
\Omega_{A/\Lambda} \otimes_A k$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
\item If $k/k'$ is separable, then $f$ is an essential surjection if
and only if the map
$\mathfrak m_B/(\mathfrak m_\Lambda B + \mathfrak m_B^2) \to
\mathfrak m_A/(\mathfrak m_\Lambda A + \mathfrak m_A^2)$
is an isomorphism.
\item If $f$ is a small extension, then $f$ is not essential if and only if
$f$ has a section $s: A \to B$ in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$
with $f \circ s = \text{id}_A$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Completion CLambda
Surjective cotangent space
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06GZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06GZ}}


Let $f: R \to S$ be a ring map in $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is surjective,
\item the map
$\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R^2 \to \mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_S^2$
is surjective, and
\item the map
$\mathfrak m_R/(\mathfrak m_\Lambda R + \mathfrak m_R^2) \to
\mathfrak m_S/(\mathfrak m_\Lambda S + \mathfrak m_S^2)$
is surjective.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: CLambdahat pushouts
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06SB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06SB}}


The category $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$ admits pushouts.

nodes.title: CLambdahat coproducts
Derivations finite
Derivations surjective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06SD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06SD}}


Let $f : R \to S$ be a morphism of $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$.
If $\text{Der}_\Lambda(S, k) \to \text{Der}_\Lambda(R, k)$ is injective,
then $f$ is surjective.

nodes.title: M adic topology
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06SE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06SE}}


Let $R$ be an object of $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$. Let $(J_n)$ be a
decreasing sequence of ideals such that $\mathfrak m_R^n \subset J_n$.
Set $J = \bigcap J_n$. Then the sequence $(J_n/J)$ defines the
$\mathfrak m_{R/J}$-adic topology on $R/J$.

nodes.title: Limit artinian
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06SF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06SF}}


Let $\ldots \to A_3 \to A_2 \to A_1$ be a sequence of surjective
ring maps in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. If
$\dim_k (\mathfrak m_{A_n}/\mathfrak m_{A_n}^2)$ is bounded, then
$S = \lim A_n$ is an object in $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$
and the ideals $I_n = \Ker(S \to A_n)$ define the
$\mathfrak m_S$-adic topology on $S$.

nodes.title: Power series
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06SG}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06SG}}


Let $R', R \in \Ob(\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda)$. Suppose that
$R = R' \oplus I$ for some ideal $I$ of $R$. Let $x_1, \ldots, x_r \in I$
map to a basis of $I/\mathfrak m_R I$. Set $S = R'[[X_1, \ldots, X_r]]$
and consider the $R'$-algebra map $S \to R$ mapping $X_i$ to $x_i$.
Assume that for every $n \gg 0$ the map
$S/\mathfrak m_S^n \to R/\mathfrak m_R^n$ has a left inverse in
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. Then $S \to R$ is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Category cofibred groupoids
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06GJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06GJ}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.  A {\it category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}$} is a category $\mathcal{F}$ equipped with a functor
$p: \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{C}$ such that $\mathcal{F}^{opp}$ is a category
fibered in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}^{opp}$ via
$p^{opp}: \mathcal{F}^{opp} \to \mathcal{C}^{opp}$.

nodes.title: Prorepresentable
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06GX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06GX}}


Let $F : \mathcal{C}_\Lambda \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
We say $F$ is {\it prorepresentable} if there exists an isomorphism
$F \cong \underline{R}|_{\mathcal{C}_\Lambda}$ of functors for some
$R \in \Ob(\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda)$.

nodes.title: Predeformation category
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06GS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06GS}}


A {\it predeformation category} $\mathcal{F}$ is a category cofibered
in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ such that $\mathcal{F}(k)$ is
equivalent to a category with a single object and a single morphism,
i.e., $\mathcal{F}(k)$ contains at least one object and there is a
unique morphism between any two objects. A {\it morphism of predeformation
categories} is a morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.

nodes.title: Formal objects
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06H3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06H3}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. The {\it category $\widehat{\mathcal{F}}$ of formal
objects of  $\mathcal{F}$} is the category with the following objects and
morphisms.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A {\it formal object $\xi = (R, \xi_n, f_n)$ of $\mathcal{F}$}
consists of an object $R$ of $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$, and a collection
indexed by $n \in \mathbf{N}$ of objects $\xi_n$ of
$\mathcal{F}(R/\mathfrak m_R^n)$ and morphisms
$f_n : \xi_{n + 1} \to \xi_n$ lying over the projection
$R/\mathfrak m_R^{n + 1} \to R/\mathfrak m_R^n$.
\item Let $\xi = (R, \xi_n, f_n)$ and $\eta = (S, \eta_n, g_n)$ be
formal objects of $\mathcal{F}$.  A {\it morphism $a : \xi \to \eta$ of
formal objects} consists of a map $a_0 : R \to S$ in
$\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$ and a collection $a_n : \xi_n \to \eta_n$
of morphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ lying over
$R/\mathfrak m_R^n \to S/\mathfrak m_S^n$,
such that for every $n$ the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\xi_{n + 1} \underset{f_n}{\longrightarrow}\underset{a_{n + 1}}{\downarrow} & \xi_n \overset{a_n}{\downarrow} \\ \eta_{n + 1} \overset{g_n}{\longrightarrow} & \eta_n\end{array}
$$
commutes.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Completion cofibred
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06H4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06H4}}


Let $p : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ be a category cofibered in
groupoids. Then
$\widehat{p} : \widehat{\mathcal{F}} \to \widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$
is a category cofibered in groupoids.

nodes.title: Completion
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06H5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06H5}}


Let $p : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ be a category cofibered in
groupoids. The category cofibered in groupoids
$\widehat{p} : \widehat{\mathcal  F} \to \widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$
is called the {\it completion of $\mathcal{F}$}.

nodes.title: Formal objects different filtration
Smooth morphism
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06HG}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06HG}}


Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a morphism of categories
cofibered in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.  We say  $\varphi$ is
{\it smooth} if it satisfies the following condition: Let $B \to A$ be
a surjective ring map in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.  Let $y \in
\Ob(\mathcal{G}(B)), x \in \Ob(\mathcal{F}(A))$, and $y
\to \varphi(x)$ be a morphism lying over $B \to A$.  Then there
exists $x' \in \Ob(\mathcal{F}(B))$, a morphism $x' \to x$
lying over $B \to A$, and a morphism $\varphi(x') \to y$ lying
over $\text{id}: B \to B$, such that the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\varphi(x') \longrightarrow\searrow & y \downarrow \\  & \varphi(x)\end{array}
$$
commutes.

nodes.title: Smoothness small extensions
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06HH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06HH}}


Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a morphism of categories
cofibered in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.  Then $\varphi$ is smooth
if the condition in Definition \ref{formal-defos-definition-smooth-morphism} is assumed to
hold only for small extensions $B \to A$.

nodes.title: Smooth morphism power series
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06HL}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06HL}}


Let $R \to S$ be a ring map in $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$. Then
the induced morphism
$\underline{S}|_{\mathcal{C}_\Lambda} \to \underline{R}|_{\mathcal{C}_\Lambda}$
is smooth if and only if $S$ is a power series ring over $R$.

nodes.title: Smooth properties
Smooth morphism essentially surjective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06HN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06HN}}


Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a smooth morphism of
categories cofibered in groupoids over $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.  Assume
$\varphi : \mathcal{F}(k) \to \mathcal{G}(k)$ is essentially surjective.
Then $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ and
$\widehat{\varphi} : \widehat{\mathcal{F}} \to \widehat{\mathcal{G}}$
are essentially surjective.

nodes.title: Versal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06HR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06HR}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids.  Let $\xi$ be a formal
object of $\mathcal{F}$ lying over $R \in \Ob(\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda)$.
We say $\xi$ is {\it versal} if the corresponding morphism
$\underline{\xi}: \underline{R}|_{\mathcal{C}_\Lambda} \to \mathcal{F}$

$F(R)$ is a one element set and that for any $M, N \in
\Ob(\text{Mod}^{fg}_R)$, the induced map
$$
F(R[M] \times_R R[N]) \to F(R[M]) \times F(R[N])

$F(R[M])$ and $G(R[M])$ are given the $R$-module structure from

We will make the link in
Section \ref{formal-defos-section-miniversal-objects-existence}.}

\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ has a minimal versal formal object satisfying
(\ref{equation-bijective}),
\item $\mathcal{F}$ has a minimal versal formal object satisfying
(\ref{equation-bijective-orbits}),
\item the following conditions hold:

nodes.title: RS associated functor
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06J8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06J8}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ satisfying (RS).
The following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\overline{\mathcal{F}}$ satisfies (RS).
\item Let $f_1: A_1 \to A$ and $f_2: A_2 \to A$ be ring maps in
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ with $f_2$ surjective. The induced map
of sets of isomorphism classes
$$
\overline{\mathcal{F}(A_1) \times_{\mathcal{F}(A)} \mathcal{F}(A_2)}
\to \overline{\mathcal{F}}(A_1) \times_{\overline{\mathcal{F}}(A)}
\overline{\mathcal{F}}(A_2)
$$

\item For every morphism $x' \to x$ in $\mathcal{F}$ lying over a
surjective ring map $A' \to A$, the map
$\text{Aut}_{A'}(x') \to \text{Aut}_A(x)$ is surjective.
\item For every morphism $x' \to x$ in $\mathcal{F}$ lying over a small
extension $A' \to A$, the map
$\text{Aut}_{A'}(x') \to \text{Aut}_A(x)$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Deformation category

\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06J9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06J9}}

satisfying (RS). A morphism of deformation categories is a morphism of
categories over $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.

nodes.title: Localize RS
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06JC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06JC}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. Let $x_0 \in \Ob(\mathcal{F}(k))$.
Let $\mathcal{F}_{x_0}$ be the category cofibred in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ constructed in
Remark \ref{formal-defos-remark-localize-cofibered-groupoid}.
If $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies (RS), then so does $\mathcal{F}_{x_0}$.
In particular, $\mathcal{F}_{x_0}$ is a deformation category.

nodes.title: RS fiber product morphisms
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06L4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06L4}}


Let
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\mathcal{H} \times_\mathcal{F} \mathcal{G} \longrightarrow\downarrow & \mathcal{G} \overset{g}{\downarrow} \\ \mathcal{H} \overset{f}{\longrightarrow} & \mathcal{F}\end{array}
$$
be $2$-fibre product of categories cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. If $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}, \mathcal{H}$
all satisfy (RS), then $\mathcal{H} \times_\mathcal{F} \mathcal{G}$
satisfies (RS).

nodes.title: Lifts
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06JE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06JE}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. Let $f: A' \to A$ be a map in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.
Let $x \in \mathcal{F}(A)$. The category $\textit{Lift}(x, f)$ of lifts of $x$
along $f$ is the category with the following objects and
morphisms.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Objects: A {\it lift of $x$ along $f$} is a morphism $x' \to x$
lying over $f$.
\item Morphisms: A {\it morphism of lifts} from $a_1 : x'_1 \to x$ to
$a_2 : x'_2 \to x$ is a morphism $b : x'_1 \to x'_2$ in
$\mathcal{F}(A')$ such that $a_2 = a_1 \circ b$.
\end{enumerate}
The set $\text{Lift}(x, f)$ of lifts of $x$ along $f$ is the set of
isomorphism classes of $\textit{Lift}(x, f)$.

nodes.title: Free transitive action
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06JI}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06JI}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a deformation category.
Let $A' \to A$ be a surjective ring map in
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ whose kernel $I$ is annihilated
by $\mathfrak m_{A'}$. Let $x \in \Ob(\mathcal{F}(A))$.
If $\text{Lift}(x, A')$ is nonempty,
then there is a free and transitive action of
$T\mathcal{F} \otimes_k I$ on $\text{Lift}(x, A')$.

nodes.title: Schlessinger prorepresentability
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06JM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06JM}}


Let $F: \mathcal{C}_\Lambda \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Then $F$ is prorepresentable if and only if
(a) $F$ is a deformation functor,
(b) $\dim_k TF$ is finite, and (c) $\gamma : \text{Der}_\Lambda(k, k) \to TF$
is injective.

nodes.title: Relative infinitesimal auts
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06JP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06JP}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over $\mathcal
C_\Lambda$. Let $x' \to x$ be a morphism in $\mathcal{F}$ lying over
$A' \to A$. The kernel
$$
\text{Inf}(x'/x) = \Ker(\text{Aut}_{A'}(x') \to \text{Aut}_A(x))
$$
is the {\it group of infinitesimal automorphisms of $x'$ over $x$}.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal auts
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06JQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06JQ}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over $\mathcal
C_\Lambda$. Let $x_0 \in \Ob(\mathcal{F}(k))$. Assume a choice of
pushforward $x_0 \to x_0'$ of $x_0$ along the map
$k \to k[\epsilon], a \mapsto a$ has been made.
Then there is a unique map $x'_0 \to x_0$ such that
$x_0 \to x_0' \to x_0$ is the identity on $x_0$.
Then
$$
\text{Inf}_{x_0}(\mathcal F) = \text{Inf}(x'_0/x_0)
$$
is the {\it group of infinitesimal automorphisms of $x_0$}

nodes.title: Automorphism functor
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06JT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06JT}}


Let $p : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids
over an arbitrary base category $\mathcal{C}$. Assume a choice of pushforwards
has been made. Let $x \in \Ob(\mathcal{F})$ and let $U = p(x)$.
Let $U/\mathcal{C}$ denote the category of objects under $U$. The
{\it automorphism functor of $x$} is the functor
$\mathit{Aut}(x) : U/\mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ sending an object
$f : U \to V$ to $\text{Aut}_V(f_*x)$ and sending a morphism
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}V' \longrightarrow &  & V \\  & U \overset{f'}{\nwarrow}\underset{f}{\nearrow} & \end{array}
$$
to the homomorphism
$\text{Aut}_{V'}(f'_*x) \to \text{Aut}_V(f_*x)$
coming from the unique morphism $f'_*x \to f_*x$ lying over
$V' \to V$ and compatible with $x \to f'_*x$ and $x \to f_*x$.

nodes.title: Aut functor RS
nodes.statement:

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ satisfying (RS). Let
$x \in \Ob(\mathcal{F}(A))$. Then
$\mathit{Aut}(x): \mathcal{C}_A \to \textit{Sets}$ satisfies (RS).

nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06JV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06JV}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ satisfying (RS). Let
$x \in \Ob(\mathcal{F}(A))$. Let $x_0$ be a pushforward of $x$ to
$\mathcal{F}(k)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $T_{\text{id}_{x_0}} \mathit{Aut}(x)$ has a natural $k$-vector
space structure such that addition agrees with composition in
$T_{\text{id}_{x_0}} \mathit{Aut}(x)$. In particular, composition in
$T_{\text{id}_{x_0}} \mathit{Aut}(x)$ is commutative.
\item There is a canonical isomorphism
$T_{\text{id}_{x_0}} \mathit{Aut}(x) \to
T_{\text{id}_{x_0}} \mathit{Aut}(x_0)$
of $k$-vector spaces.
\end{enumerate}

$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ satisfying (RS). Let $x' \to x$ be a
morphism lying over a surjective ring map $A' \to A$ with kernel $I$
annihilated by $\mathfrak m_{A'}$. Let $x_0$ be a pushforward of $x$ to

nodes.title: Infaut trivial

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ satisfying (RS). Let
$x_0 \in \Ob(\mathcal{F}(k))$. Then $\text{Inf}_{x_0}(\mathcal{F}) = 0$
if and only if the natural morphism
$\mathcal{F}_{x_0} \to \overline{\mathcal{F}_{x_0}}$ of
categories cofibered in groupoids is an equivalence.

nodes.title: Deformation categories fiber product morphisms
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06L5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06L5}}


Let $f : \mathcal{H} \to \mathcal{F}$ and $g : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$
be $1$-morphisms of deformation categories. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{H} \times_\mathcal{F} \mathcal{G}$ is a
deformation category, and
\item we have a $6$-term exact sequence of vector spaces
$$
0 \to \text{Inf}(\mathcal{W})
\to \text{Inf}(\mathcal{H}) \oplus \text{Inf}(\mathcal{G})
\to \text{Inf}(\mathcal{F}) \to
T\mathcal{W} \to T\mathcal{H} \oplus T\mathcal{G} \to T\mathcal{F}
$$
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Map fibre products smooth
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DYN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DYN}}


Let $\mathcal{H}_1 \to \mathcal{G}$, $\mathcal{H}_2 \to \mathcal{G}$, and
$\mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ be maps of categories cofibred in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ are deformation categories,
\item $T\mathcal{G} \to T\mathcal{F}$ is injective, and
\item $\text{Inf}(\mathcal{G}) \to \text{Inf}(\mathcal{F})$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{H}_1 \times_\mathcal{G} \mathcal{H}_2 \to
\mathcal{H}_1 \times_\mathcal{F} \mathcal{H}_2$ is smooth.

nodes.title: Easy check smooth
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DYP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DYP}}


Let $f : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map of deformation
categories. Let $x_0 \in \Ob(\mathcal{F}(k))$ with image
$y_0 \in \Ob(\mathcal{G}(k))$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item the map $T\mathcal{F} \to T\mathcal{G}$ is surjective, and
\item for every small extension $A' \to A$ in $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$
and $x \in \mathcal{F}(A)$ with image $y \in \mathcal{G}(A)$
if there is a lift of $y$ to $A'$, then there is a lift
of $x$ to $A'$,
\end{enumerate}
then $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ is smooth (and vice versa).

nodes.title: Map between smooth
Groupoid in functors
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06K3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06K3}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. The
{\it category of groupoids in functors on $\mathcal{C}$}
is the category with the following objects and morphisms.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Objects: A {\it groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}$} is a quintuple
$(U, R, s, t, c)$ where $U, R : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ are
functors and $s, t : R \to U$ and $c : R \times_{s, U, t} R \to R$
are morphisms with the following property: For any object $T$ of $\mathcal{C}$,
the quintuple
$$
(U(T), R(T), s, t, c)
$$
is a groupoid category.
\item Morphisms: A {\it morphism $(U, R, s, t, c) \to (U', R', s', t', c')$ of
groupoids in functors on $\mathcal{C}$} consists of morphisms $U \to U'$
and $R \to R'$ with the following property: For any object $T$ of
$\mathcal{C}$, the induced maps $U(T) \to U'(T)$ and
$R(T) \to R'(T)$ define a functor between groupoid categories
$$
(U(T), R(T), s, t, c) \to (U'(T), R'(T), s', t', c').
$$
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Representable
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06K6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06K6}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. A groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}$ is
{\it representable} if it is isomorphic to one of the form
$(\underline{U}, \underline{R}, s, t, c)$ where $U$ and $R$ are objects of
$\mathcal{C}$ and the pushout $R \amalg_{s, U, t} R$ exists.

nodes.title: Restricting groupoids in functors
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06K9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06K9}}


Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a groupoid in functors on a category $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{C}'$ be a subcategory of $\mathcal{C}$. The
{\it restriction $(U, R, s, t, c)|_{\mathcal{C}'}$ of $(U, R, s, t, c)$
to $\mathcal{C}'$} is the groupoid
in functors on $\mathcal{C}'$ given by $(U|_{\mathcal{C}'}, R|_{\mathcal
C'}, s|_{\mathcal{C}'}, t|_{\mathcal{C}'}, c|_{\mathcal{C}'})$.

nodes.title: Quotient
Prorepresentable groupoid in functors
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06KD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06KD}}


A groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ is {\it prorepresentable}
if it is isomorphic to
$(\underline{R_0}, \underline{R_1}, s, t, c)|_{\mathcal{C}_\Lambda}$
for some representable groupoid in functors
$(\underline{R_0}, \underline{R_1}, s, t, c)$ on the category
$\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$.

nodes.title: Completion groupoid in functors
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06KE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06KE}}


Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.
The {\it completion $(U, R, s, t, c)^{\wedge}$ of $(U, R, s, t, c)$} is the
groupoid in functors
$(\widehat{U}, \widehat{R}, \widehat{s}, \widehat{t}, \widehat{c})$
on $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$ described above.

nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06KU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06KU}}


Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a smooth groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$.
Assume $U$ and $R$ are deformation functors. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The quotient $[U/R]$ is a deformation category.
\item The tangent space of $[U/R]$ is
$$
T[U/R] = \Coker(ds-dt: TR \to TU).
$$
\item The space of infinitesimal automorphisms of $[U/R]$ is
$$
\text{Inf}([U/R]) =
\Ker(ds \oplus dt : TR \to TU \oplus TU).
$$
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Presentation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06KX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06KX}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over a category
$\mathcal{C}$. Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a groupoid in functors on
$\mathcal{C}$. A
{\it presentation of $\mathcal{F}$ by $(U, R, s, t, c)$} is an equivalence
$\varphi : [U/R] \to \mathcal{F}$ of categories cofibered in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}$.

nodes.title: Presentation construction
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06KY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06KY}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be category cofibered in groupoids over a category
$\mathcal{C}$. Let $U : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Let $f : U \to \mathcal{F}$ be a morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}$. Define $R, s, t, c$ as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ is the functor
$U \times_{f, \mathcal{F}, f} U$.
\item $t, s : R \to U$ are the first and second projections,
respectively.
\item $c : R \times_{s, U, t} R \to R$ is the morphism given by projection
onto the first and last factors of
$U \times_{f, \mathcal{F}, f} U \times_{f, \mathcal{F}, f} U$
under the canonical isomorphism
$R \times_{s, U, t} R \to
U \times_{f, \mathcal{F}, f} U \times_{f, \mathcal{F}, f} U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $(U, R, s, t, c)$ is a groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}$.

nodes.title: Presentation morphism
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06KZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06KZ}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be category cofibered in groupoids over a category
$\mathcal{C}$. Let $U : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Let $f : U \to \mathcal{F}$ be a morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids
over $\mathcal{C}$. Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be the groupoid in functors on
$\mathcal{C}$ constructed from $f : U \to \mathcal{F}$ in
Lemma \ref{formal-defos-lemma-presentation-construction}.
Then there is a natural morphism $[f] : [U/R] \to \mathcal{F}$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $[f]: [U/R] \to \mathcal{F}$ is fully faithful.
\item $[f]: [U/R] \to \mathcal{F}$ is an equivalence if and only if
$f : U \to \mathcal{F}$ is essentially surjective.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Smooth groupoid in functors construction
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06L1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06L1}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. Let $U : \mathcal{C}_\Lambda \to \textit{Sets}$
be a functor. Let $f : U \to \mathcal{F}$ be a smooth morphism of
categories cofibered in groupoids. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $(U, R, s, t, c)$ is the groupoid in functors on
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ constructed from $f : U \to \mathcal{F}$ in
Lemma \ref{formal-defos-lemma-presentation-construction}, then $(U, R, s, t, c)$
is smooth.
\item If $f : U(k) \to \mathcal{F}(k)$ is essentially surjective,
then the morphism $[f] : [U/R] \to \mathcal{F}$ of
Lemma \ref{formal-defos-lemma-presentation-morphism}
is an equivalence.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Deformation functor diagonal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06L6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06L6}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a deformation category.
Let $U : \mathcal{C}_\Lambda \to \textit{Sets}$ be a deformation functor.
Let $f: U \to \mathcal{F}$ be a morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids.
Then $U \times_{f, \mathcal{F}, f} U$ is a deformation functor
with tangent space fitting into an exact sequence of $k$-vector spaces
$$
0 \to \text{Inf}(\mathcal{F}) \to
T(U \times_{f, \mathcal{F}, f} U) \to TU \oplus TU
$$

nodes.title: Prorepresentable groupoid in functors construction
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06L7}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06L7}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a deformation category.
Let $U : \mathcal{C}_\Lambda \to \textit{Sets}$ be a prorepresentable functor.
Let $f : U \to \mathcal{F}$ be a morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids.
Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be the groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$
constructed from $f : U \to \mathcal{F}$ in
Lemma \ref{formal-defos-lemma-presentation-construction}. If
$\dim_k \text{Inf}(\mathcal{F}) < \infty$, then
$(U, R, s, t, c)$ is prorepresentable.

Let $U: \mathcal{C}_\Lambda \to \textit{Sets}$ be a

nodes.title: Minimal prorepresentable groupoid autoequivalence
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06KQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06KQ}}


Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a minimal smooth prorepresentable groupoid in
functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. If $\varphi : [U/R] \to [U/R]$ is an
equivalence of categories cofibered in groupoids, then $\varphi$ is an
isomorphism.

nodes.title: Minimal prorepresentable groupoid equivalence
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06KR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06KR}}


Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ and $(U', R', s', t', c')$ be minimal smooth
prorepresentable groupoids in functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. If
$\varphi : [U/R] \to [U'/R']$ is an equivalence of categories cofibered
in groupoids, then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Minimal groupoid in functors construction
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06L2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06L2}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a deformation category such that
$\dim_k T\mathcal{F} <\infty$ and
$\dim_k \text{Inf}(\mathcal{F}) < \infty$.
Then there exists a minimal versal formal object $\xi$ of $\mathcal{F}$.
Say $\xi$ lies over $R \in \Ob(\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda)$.
Let $U = \underline{R}|_{\mathcal{C}_\Lambda}$.
Let $f = \underline{\xi} : U \to \mathcal{F}$ be the associated
morphism. Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be the groupoid in functors on
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ constructed from $f : U \to \mathcal{F}$ in
Lemma \ref{formal-defos-lemma-presentation-construction}.
Then $(U, R, s, t, c)$ is a minimal smooth prorepresentable
groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$ and there
is an equivalence $[U/R] \to \mathcal{F}$.

nodes.title: Minimal presentations equivalent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06L3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06L3}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. Assume there exist presentations of
$\mathcal{F}$ by minimal smooth prorepresentable groupoids
in functors $(U, R, s, t, c)$ and $(U', R', s', t', c')$.
Then $(U, R, s, t, c)$ and $(U', R', s', t', c')$ are isomorphic.

nodes.title: Minimal smooth prorepresentable presentations
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06TE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06TE}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a category cofibered in groupoids over
$\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$. Consider the following conditions
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ admits a presentation by a normalized
smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ admits a presentation by a
smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ admits a presentation by a minimal
smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the following conditions
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a deformation category.
\item $\dim_k T\mathcal{F}$ is finite.
\item $\dim_k \text{Inf}(\mathcal{F})$ is finite.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then (2), (3), (4) are equivalent and are implied by (1).
If $k' \subset k$ is separable, then (1), (2), (3), (4) are all equivalent.
Furthermore, the minimal smooth prorepresentable groupoids in functors
which provide a presentation of $\mathcal{F}$ are unique up to isomorphism.

nodes.title: Homotopy
Composition homotopic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DQC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DQC}}


In the category $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$, if $f_1, f_2 : R \to S$
are formally homotopic and $g : S \to S'$ is a morphism, then
$g \circ f_1$ and $g \circ f_2$ are formally homotopic.

nodes.title: Versal unique up to homotopy
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DQD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DQD}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a deformation category over $\mathcal{C}_\Lambda$
with $\dim_k T\mathcal{F} < \infty$ and
$\dim_k \text{Inf}(\mathcal{F}) < \infty$. Let $\xi$ be a versal formal
object lying over $R$. Let $\eta$ be a formal object lying over $S$.
Then any two maps
$$
f, g : R \to S
$$
such that $f_*\xi \cong \eta \cong g_*\xi$ are formally homotopic.

nodes.title: Homotopic minimal prime
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DQE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DQE}}


In the category $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}_\Lambda$, if $f_1, f_2 : R \to S$
are formally homotopic and $\mathfrak p \subset R$ is a minimal
prime ideal, then $f_1(\mathfrak p)S = f_2(\mathfrak p)S$ as ideals.

nodes.title: Situation: Change of fields
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07W8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 07W8}}


Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let $\Lambda \to k \to l$ be a finite
ring maps where $k$ and $l$ are fields. Thus $l/k$ is a finite
extensions of fields. A typical object of $\mathcal{C}_{\Lambda, l}$ will be
denoted $B$ and a typical object of $\mathcal{C}_{\Lambda, k}$ will be
denoted $A$. We define
\begin{equation}
\label{equation-comparison}
\mathcal{C}_{\Lambda, l} \longrightarrow \mathcal{C}_{\Lambda, k},
\quad
B \longmapsto B \times_l k
\end{equation}
Given a category cofibred in groupoids
$p : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{C}_{\Lambda, k}$ we obtain
an associated category cofibred in groupoids
$$
p_{l/k} : \mathcal{F}_{l/k} \longrightarrow \mathcal{C}_{\Lambda, l}
$$
by setting $\mathcal{F}_{l/k}(B) = \mathcal{F}(B \times_l k)$.

nodes.title: Elementary properties change of field

With notation and assumptions as in Situation \ref{formal-defos-situation-change-of-fields}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item We have $\overline{\mathcal{F}_{l/k}} = (\overline{\mathcal{F}})_{l/k}$.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is a predeformation category, then $\mathcal{F}_{l/k}$
is a predeformation category.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies (S1), then $\mathcal{F}_{l/k}$
satisfies (S1).
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies (S2), then $\mathcal{F}_{l/k}$
satisfies (S2).
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies (RS), then $\mathcal{F}_{l/k}$
satisfies (RS).
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Standard resolution
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08PM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08PM}}


Let $A \to B$ be a ring map. The {\it standard resolution of $B$ over $A$}
is the augmentation $\epsilon : P_\bullet \to B$ with terms
$$
P_0 = A[B],\quad P_1 = A[A[B]],\quad \ldots
$$

Simplicial, Example \ref{simplicial-example-polynomial-algebra-maps}.

nodes.statement:

is the complex of $B$-modules associated to the simplicial $B$-module
$$
\Omega_{P_\bullet/A} \otimes_{P_\bullet, \epsilon} B
$$
where $\epsilon : P_\bullet \to B$ is the standard resolution
of $B$ over $A$.

nodes.statement:

Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $A \to B$ be a finite type ring map.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the category of $A$-algebra maps $C \to B$. Let
$n \geq 0$ and let $P_\bullet$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{A}$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P_\bullet \to B$ is a trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets,
\item $P_k$ is finite type over $A$ for $k \leq n$,

nodes.title: Pi shriek finite
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08PY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08PY}}


Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $A \to B$ be a finite type ring map.
Let $\pi$, $\underline{B}$ be as in (\ref{equation-pi}).
If $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\underline{B}$-module such that
$\mathcal{F}(P, \alpha)$ is a finite $B$-module for all
$\alpha : P = A[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to B$, then the cohomology modules
of $L\pi_!(\mathcal{F})$ are finite $B$-modules.

nodes.title: Cotangent finite
O homology B homology
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08QJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08QJ}}


Let $A \to B$ be a ring map. Let $\pi$, $\mathcal{O}$, $\underline{B}$
be as in (\ref{equation-pi}). For any $\mathcal{O}$-module $\mathcal{F}$
we have
$$
L\pi_!(\mathcal{F}) = L\pi_!(Li^*\mathcal{F}) =
L\pi_!(\mathcal{F} \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \underline{B})
$$
in $D(\textit{Ab})$.

nodes.title: Apply O B comparison
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08QK}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08QK}}


Let $A \to B$ be a ring map. Let $\pi$, $\mathcal{O}$, $\underline{B}$
be as in (\ref{equation-pi}). We have
$$
L\pi_!(\mathcal{O}) = L\pi_!(\underline{B}) = B
\quad\text{and}\quad
L_{B/A} = L\pi_!(\Omega_{\mathcal{O}/A} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \underline{B}) =
L\pi_!(\Omega_{\mathcal{O}/A})
$$
in $D(\textit{Ab})$.

nodes.title: Special case triangle
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SA}}


Let $A \to B \to C$ be ring maps. If $B$ is a polynomial algebra over
$A$, then there is a distinguished triangle
$L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} C \to L_{C/A} \to L_{C/B} \to
L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} C[1]$ in $D(C)$.

nodes.title: Flat base change
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08QP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08QP}}


Assume (\ref{equation-commutative-square}) induces a quasi-isomorphism
$B \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' = B'$. Then, with notation as in
(\ref{equation-double-square}) and
$\mathcal{F}' \in \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}')$,
we have $L\pi_!(g^{-1}\mathcal{F}') = L\pi'_!(\mathcal{F}')$.

nodes.title: Flat base change cotangent complex
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08QQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08QQ}}


If (\ref{equation-commutative-square}) induces a quasi-isomorphism
$B \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' = B'$, then the functoriality map
induces an isomorphism
$$
L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} B' \longrightarrow L_{B'/A'}
$$

nodes.title: Cotangent complex product
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SC}}


Let $A \to B$ and $A \to C$ be ring maps.
Then the map $L_{B \times C/A} \to L_{B/A} \oplus L_{C/A}$ is
an isomorphism in $D(B \times C)$.

nodes.title: Triangle ses
Polynomial on top
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08QV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08QV}}


With notation as in (\ref{equation-three-maps})
suppose that $C$ is a polynomial algebra over $B$. Then
$L\pi_!(g_3^{-1}\mathcal{F}) = L\pi_{3, !}\mathcal{F} = \pi_{3, !}\mathcal{F}$
for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}_{C/B}$

nodes.title: Triangle compute lower shriek
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08QW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08QW}}


With notation as in (\ref{equation-three-maps}) we have
$Lg_{i, !} \circ g_i^{-1} = \text{id}$ for $i = 1, 2, 3$
and hence also $L\pi_! \circ g_i^{-1} = L\pi_{i, !}$ for
$i = 1, 2, 3$.

nodes.title: Triangle
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08QX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08QX}}


Let $A \to B \to C$ be ring maps. There is a canonical distinguished
triangle
$$
L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} C \to L_{C/A} \to L_{C/B} \to
L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} C[1]
$$
in $D(C)$.

nodes.title: Localize at bottom
Derived diagonal
Bootstrap
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08R1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08R1}}


Let $A \to B$ be a ring map such that $\text{Tor}^A_i(B, B) = 0$ for $i > 0$
and such that $L_{B/B \otimes_A B} = 0$.
Then $L_{B/A} = 0$ in $D(B)$.

nodes.title: When zero
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08R2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08R2}}


The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}$ is zero in each of the following cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to B$ and $B \otimes_A B \to B$ are flat, i.e., $A \to B$
is weakly \'etale
(More on Algebra, Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-weakly-etale}),
\item $A \to B$ is a flat epimorphism of rings,
\item $B = S^{-1}A$ for some multiplicative subset $S \subset A$,
\item $A \to B$ is unramified and flat,
\item $A \to B$ is \'etale,
\item $A \to B$ is a filtered colimit of ring maps for which
the cotangent complex vanishes,
\item $B$ is a henselization of a local ring of $A$,
\item $B$ is a strict henselization of a local ring of $A$, and
\item add more here.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Localize on top
Localize
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SF}}


Let $A \to B$ be ring maps and $S \subset A$, $T \subset B$ multiplicative
subsets such that $S$ maps into $T$.
Then $L_{T^{-1}B/S^{-1}A} = L_{B/A} \otimes_B T^{-1}B$
in $D(T^{-1}B)$.

nodes.title: Cotangent complex henselization
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08UN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08UN}}


Let $A \to B$ be a local ring homomorphism of local rings.
Let $A^h \to B^h$, resp.\ $A^{sh} \to B^{sh}$ be the induced
maps of henselizations, resp.\ strict henselizations.
Then
$$
L_{B^h/A^h} = L_{B^h/A} = L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} B^h
\quad\text{resp.}\quad
L_{B^{sh}/A^{sh}} = L_{B^{sh}/A} = L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} B^{sh}
$$
in $D(B^h)$, resp.\ $D(B^{sh})$.

nodes.title: When projective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08R5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08R5}}


If $A \to B$ is a smooth ring map, then $L_{B/A} = \Omega_{B/A}[0]$.

nodes.title: Frobenius homotopy
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G5Y}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G5Y}}


Let $A \to B$ be a ring map with $p = 0$ in $A$. Let $P_\bullet$ be the
standard resolution of $B$ over $A$. The map $P_\bullet \to P_\bullet$
induced by the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}B \underset{F_B}{\longrightarrow} & B \\ A \uparrow\overset{F_A}{\longrightarrow} & A \uparrow\end{array}
$$
discussed in Section \ref{cotangent-section-functoriality} is homotopic to the Frobenius
endomorphism $P_\bullet \to P_\bullet$ given by Frobenius on each $P_n$.

nodes.title: Frobenius acts as zero
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G5Z}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G5Z}}


Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A \to B$ be a ring homomorphism
and assume that $p = 0$ in $A$. The map $L_{B/A} \to L_{B/A}$
of Section \ref{cotangent-section-functoriality} induced by the
Frobenius maps $F_A$ and $F_B$ is homotopic to zero.

nodes.title: Perfect zero
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G60}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G60}}


Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A \to B$ be a ring homomorphism
and assume that $p = 0$ in $A$. If $A$ and $B$ are perfect, then
$L_{B/A}$ is zero in $D(B)$.

nodes.title: The cohomology of the cotangent complex of a surjective ring map is trivial in degree z...
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08RA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08RA}}



Let $A \to B$ be a surjective ring map with kernel $I$.
Then $H^0(L_{B/A}) = 0$ and $H^{-1}(L_{B/A}) = I/I^2$.
This isomorphism comes from the map (\ref{equation-comparison-map})
for the object $(A \to B)$ of $\mathcal{C}_{B/A}$.

nodes.title: Relation with naive cotangent complex
Vanishing symmetric powers
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08RD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08RD}}


Notation and assumptions as in
Cohomology on Sites, Example \ref{sites-cohomology-example-category-to-point}.
Assume $\mathcal{C}$ has a cosimplicial object as in
Cohomology on Sites, Lemma
\ref{sites-cohomology-lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution}.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a flat $\underline{B}$-module such that
$H_0(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}) = 0$.
Then $H_l(\mathcal{C}, \text{Sym}_{\underline{B}}^k(\mathcal{F})) = 0$
for $l < k$.

nodes.title: Map tors zero
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08RE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08RE}}


Let $A$ be a ring. Let $P = A[E]$ be a polynomial ring.
Set $I = (e; e \in E) \subset P$. The maps
$\text{Tor}_i^P(A, I^{n + 1}) \to \text{Tor}_i^P(A, I^n)$
are zero for all $i$ and $n$.

nodes.title: Quillen spectral sequence
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08RF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08RF}}


Let $A \to B$ be a surjective ring map. Consider the sheaf
$\Omega = \Omega_{\mathcal{O}/A} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \underline{B}$ of
$\underline{B}$-modules on $\mathcal{C}_{B/A}$, see
Section \ref{cotangent-section-compute-L-pi-shriek}.
Then there is a spectral sequence with $E_1$-page
$$
E_1^{p, q} =
H_{- p - q}(\mathcal{C}_{B/A}, \text{Sym}^p_{\underline{B}}(\Omega))
\Rightarrow \text{Tor}^A_{- p - q}(B, B)
$$
with $d_r$ of bidegree $(r, -r + 1)$.
Moreover, $H_i(\mathcal{C}_{B/A}, \text{Sym}^k_{\underline{B}}(\Omega)) = 0$
for $i < k$.

nodes.title: Biderivation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09CE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09CE}}


Let $A \to B$ be a ring map. Let $M$ be a $(B, B)$-bimodule
over $A$. An {\it $A$-biderivation} is an $A$-linear map $\lambda : B \to M$
such that $\lambda(xy) = x\lambda(y) + \lambda(x)y$.

nodes.title: Polynomial ring unique
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09CF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09CF}}


Let $P = A[S]$ be a polynomial ring over $A$. Let $M$ be a $(P, P)$-bimodule
over $A$. Given $m_s \in M$ for $s \in S$, there exists a unique
$A$-biderivation $\lambda : P \to M$ mapping $s$ to $m_s$ for $s \in S$.

nodes.title: Compare higher
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09CG}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09CG}}


In the situation above denote $L$ the complex
(\ref{equation-lichtenbaum-schlessinger}).
There is a canonical map $L_{B/A} \to L$ in $D(B)$ which
induces an isomorphism $\tau_{\geq -2}L_{B/A} \to L$ in $D(B)$.

nodes.title: Special case
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SI}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SI}}


Let $A = \mathbf{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to B = \mathbf{Z}$
be the ring map which sends $x_i$ to $0$ for $i = 1, \ldots, n$.
Let $I = (x_1, \ldots, x_n) \subset A$. Then $L_{B/A}$ is quasi-isomorphic to
$I/I^2[1]$.

nodes.title: Mod regular sequence
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SJ}}


Let $A \to B$ be a surjective ring map whose kernel $I$ is generated
by a Koszul-regular sequence (for example a regular sequence).
Then $L_{B/A}$ is quasi-isomorphic to $I/I^2[1]$.

nodes.title: Mod Koszul regular ideal
Cotangent complex local complete intersection
Tensor product tor independent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09DA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09DA}}


If $A$ and $B$ are Tor independent $R$-algebras, then the object $E$
in (\ref{equation-tensor-product}) is zero. In this case we have
$$
L_{A \otimes_R B/R} =
L_{A/R} \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} (A \otimes_R B) \oplus
L_{B/R} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} (A \otimes_R B)
$$
which is represented by the complex
$L_{A/R} \otimes_R B \oplus L_{B/R} \otimes_R A $
of $A \otimes_R B$-modules.

nodes.title: Tensor product
Find obstruction
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SP}}


In the situation above we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a canonical element $\xi \in \Ext^2_B(L_{B/A}, N)$
whose vanishing is a sufficient and necessary condition for the existence
of a solution to (\ref{equation-to-solve}).
\item If there exists a solution, then the set of
isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under
$\Ext^1_B(L_{B/A}, N)$.
\item Given a solution $B'$, the set of automorphisms of $B'$
fitting into (\ref{equation-to-solve}) is canonically isomorphic
to $\Ext^0_B(L_{B/A}, N)$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Atiyah class
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09DE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09DE}}


Let $A \to B$ be a ring map. Let $M$ be a $B$-module.
The map $M \to L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} M[1]$
in (\ref{equation-atiyah}) is called the {\it Atiyah class} of $M$.

nodes.title: Standard resolution sheaves rings
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SR}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings
on $\mathcal{C}$. The {\it standard resolution of $\mathcal{B}$ over
$\mathcal{A}$} is the augmentation
$\epsilon : \mathcal{P}_\bullet \to \mathcal{B}$
with terms
$$
\mathcal{P}_0 = \mathcal{A}[\mathcal{B}],\quad
\mathcal{P}_1 = \mathcal{A}[\mathcal{A}[\mathcal{B}]],\quad \ldots
$$
and maps as constructed above.

nodes.title: Cotangent complex morphism sheaves rings
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SS}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings
on $\mathcal{C}$.
The {\it cotangent complex} $L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}}$
is the complex of $\mathcal{B}$-modules associated to the
simplicial module
$$
\Omega_{\mathcal{P}_\bullet/\mathcal{A}}
\otimes_{\mathcal{P}_\bullet, \epsilon} \mathcal{B}
$$
where $\epsilon : \mathcal{P}_\bullet \to \mathcal{B}$
is the standard resolution of $\mathcal{B}$ over
$\mathcal{A}$. We usually think of $L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}}$
as an object of $D(\mathcal{B})$.

nodes.title: Pullback cotangent morphism topoi
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SV}}


Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a morphism of topoi.
Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings
on $\mathcal{C}$. Then
$f^{-1}L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}} = L_{f^{-1}\mathcal{B}/f^{-1}\mathcal{A}}$.

nodes.title: Compute L morphism sheaves rings
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SW}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a
homomorphism of sheaves of rings on $\mathcal{C}$. Then
$H^i(L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}})$ is the sheaf associated to the
presheaf $U \mapsto H^i(L_{\mathcal{B}(U)/\mathcal{A}(U)})$.

nodes.title: H0 L morphism sheaves rings
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08UR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08UR}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a
homomorphism of sheaves of rings on $\mathcal{C}$. Then
$H^0(L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}}) = \Omega_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}}$.

nodes.title: Compute L product sheaves rings
Triangle sheaves rings
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08SZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08SZ}}


Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{C}$
be homomorphisms of sheaves of rings on $\mathcal{D}$.
There is a canonical distinguished triangle
$$
L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}} \otimes_\mathcal{B}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{C}
\to L_{\mathcal{C}/\mathcal{A}} \to L_{\mathcal{C}/\mathcal{B}} \to
L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}} \otimes_\mathcal{B}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{C}[1]
$$
in $D(\mathcal{C})$.

nodes.title: Stalk cotangent complex
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08T0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08T0}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a
homomorphism of sheaves of rings on $\mathcal{C}$. If $p$ is a point
of $\mathcal{C}$, then
$(L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}})_p = L_{\mathcal{B}_p/\mathcal{A}_p}$.

nodes.title: Compare cotangent complex with naive
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08US}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08US}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a
homomorphism of sheaves of rings on $\mathcal{C}$.
There is a canonical map
$L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}} \to \NL_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}}$
which identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation
$\tau_{\geq -1}L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}}$.

nodes.title: Atiyah class general
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09DI}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09DI}}


Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{B}$-modules.
The map $\mathcal{F} \to
L_{\mathcal{B}/\mathcal{A}} \otimes_\mathcal{B}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{F}[1]$
in (\ref{equation-atiyah-general}) is called the {\it Atiyah class} of
$\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.title: Cotangent complex morphism ringed spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08UU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08UU}}


Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (S, \mathcal{O}_S)$ be a morphism of
ringed spaces. The {\it cotangent complex} $L_f$ of $f$ is
$L_f = L_{\mathcal{O}_X/f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_S}$.
We will also use the notation
$L_f = L_{X/S} = L_{\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{O}_S}$.

nodes.title: H0 L morphism ringed spaces
Triangle ringed spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08T4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08T4}}


Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms of ringed spaces.
Then there is a canonical distinguished triangle
$$
Lf^* L_{Y/Z} \to L_{X/Z} \to L_{X/Y} \to Lf^*L_{Y/Z}[1]
$$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

nodes.title: Compare cotangent complex with naive ringed spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08UW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08UW}}


Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism of
ringed spaces. There is a canonical map $L_{X/Y} \to \NL_{X/Y}$ which
identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation
$\tau_{\geq -1}L_{X/Y}$.

nodes.title: Find obstruction ringed spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08UZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 08UZ}}


In the situation above we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a canonical element
$\xi \in \Ext^2_{\mathcal{O}_X}(L_{X/S}, \mathcal{G})$
whose vanishing is a sufficient and necessary condition for the existence
of a solution to (\ref{equation-to-solve-ringed-spaces}).
\item If there exists a solution, then the set of
isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under
$\Ext^1_{\mathcal{O}_X}(L_{X/S}, \mathcal{G})$.
